page: List of tallest buildings in Dallas

rows.text: Tallest building completed in Dallas in the 1980s.

Tallest building completed in Dallas in the 1970s. Originally built as the First International Building at a height of 710 ft (216 m). It underwent a major renovation in 1986, which increased its height to 886 ft (270 m).
Mixed-use office, residential, and hotel building.
Also known as Chase Arts Tower since 2023.
Mixed-use office, residential, and hotel building.
Also known as the Sinclair Residences. Mixed-use office and residential building.
Also known as The National. Tallest building completed in Dallas in the 1960s. Mixed-use residential, hotel, and office building.

Tallest building completed in Dallas in the 1950s. Also known as Republic Center Tower I. Formerly known as Republic National Bank Building. Tallest fully residential building in Dallas since its renovation in 2007.
Not a habitable building; included for comparison purposes.
Tallest building in the city outside of Downtown Dallas.
Tallest building completed in Dallas in the 2010s.

Tallest building completed in Dallas in the 1940s. The only major office building completed in the US during World War II. Originally built to a height of 430 ft (131 m) in 1943, it was increased to 523 ft (159 m) during a renovation in 1958. Now a mixed-use office and residential building.
Originally built as an office building, now a mixed-use office and residential building.
Tallest building completed in Dallas in the 2000s. Mixed-use hotel and residential building.
Originally an office building. Vacant from 1992 to 2004, when it was converted to a residential building.
Tallest building completed in Dallas in the 1920s. Originally an office building.
Also known as The Katy Victory Park or Katy Station.
Formerly known as the Mercantile Commerce Building. Originally an office building until it was renovated in 2016.

rows.text: Bank of America Tower at Parkside

tables.section: Tallest under construction or proposed > Proposed

rows.text: Approved in 2021. Will replace Republic Center Tower II as the 12th-tallest building in Dallas. Despite approval, there are no signs of construction.
Planned as a twin tower to the Bank of America Plaza. Cancelled due to the collapse of the oil and real estate market in Texas during the mid-1980s.
The project was approaching its groundbreaking in 1970, but was cancelled after the major hotel operator, Harvey Hotels, withdrew from the venture.
Now built as AMLI Fountain Place.
Construction began in 2007, but in March 2008, the city failed to approve the project, the construction crane was dismantled, and the site was whitewashed with no further progress.
Planned as a twin tower to the Cityplace Tower. Cancelled due to the economic downturn in 1980s.
Was later extended to 493 ft (150 m) in 1934
Was later extended to 523 ft (159 m) in 1958
Was later extended to 886 ft (270 m) in 1986
